description: Nearest rich galaxy cluster; R_200 ~2.2 Mpc (Mei et al. 2007 SBF distance, Strauss & Willick 1995 extent). The named Virgo Cluster includes the M84/M86 Markarian Chain and M49 subgroups, spanning ~12° on the sky with ~7 Mpc line-of-sight extent.
Second-nearest rich cluster; R_200 ~1.4 Mpc. The Fornax Cluster region of Drinkwater et al. 2000 (PASA 17, 227) maps the outer cluster and Fornax II group to ~3 Mpc.
Moderately rich cluster; R_200 ~1.5 Mpc (Richter 1989). Named extent ~3 Mpc covers the outer A1060 membership; the cluster sits in the wider Hydra Wall filament.
X-ray luminous cluster; R_200 ~1.6 Mpc (Lucey et al. 1986). Named extent ~4 Mpc spans the Cen30 (NGC 4696) and Cen45 (NGC 4709) subgroups (Stein 1996, A&AS 116, 203).
Massive cluster at the Great Attractor; R_200 ~1.5 Mpc. Kraan-Korteweg et al. 1996 reconstruction places the outer membership at ~2–3 Mpc through the Zone of Avoidance.

One of the X-ray brightest clusters; R_200 ~2.0 Mpc (Simionescu 2011). Walker et al. 2012 (ApJ 745, L21) map X-ray emission to ~2 R_200; the named Perseus Cluster region includes the chain through NGC 1275.
Archetype rich cluster; R_200 ~3.0 Mpc weak-lensing (Kubo et al. 2007). Named extent ~6 Mpc includes the NGC 4839 infalling southwest group (Neumann et al. 2003, A&A 400, 811).
Relaxed cool-core cluster with BCG NGC 6166; R_200 ~2.0 Mpc. Part of the A2197/A2199 interacting pair whose combined infall pattern extends to ~4 Mpc (Rines et al. 2001, ApJ 561, L41).
Hot, X-ray luminous cluster adjacent to the Zone of Avoidance; R_200 ~2.0 Mpc (Watanabe 2001). X-ray envelope extends well past R_200 per Million et al. 2010 (MNRAS 407, 2046).

Unrelaxed, substructured cluster; R_200 ~1.8 Mpc (Bird, Davis & Beers 1995). Sánchez-Janssen et al. 2005 (A&A 434, 521) map the irregular membership envelope to ~3–4 Mpc; forms a triplet with A2147 and A2152.
Brightest cluster at the core of the Shapley Concentration; R_200 ~2.5 Mpc (Reiprich & Böhringer 2002). Named extent ~5 Mpc covers the wider A3558 outer-membership envelope.
Irregular, actively merging cluster that forms the Leo–Coma double with A1656 at ~100 Mpc; Gregory & Thompson 1978 (ApJ 222, 784) identified the Coma/A1367 supercluster around this pair.
Massive, relaxed cool-core cluster at z~0.077 with BCG IC 1101; among the most X-ray luminous clusters within 400 Mpc and a standard calibrator for the cluster mass–luminosity relation.
Massive X-ray luminous cluster in the outer Shapley Concentration; one of the brightest clusters in the ROSAT All-Sky Survey (Markevitch et al. 1998).
A double-cluster merger system at z~0.073 near the core of the Corona Borealis Supercluster; Chandra imaging reveals ongoing infall of the two subclusters.
Our home supercluster; the gravitational basin-of-attraction centre lies near the Norma/Great-Attractor direction at ~80 Mpc, spanning ~160 Mpc end-to-end (Tully et al. 2014, Nature 513, 71).
A prominent ~70 Mpc-long filament spanning Perseus, Pisces, A262, and A347; a textbook example of large-scale structure since Haynes & Giovanelli 1986 (ApJ 306, 466).
~30 Mpc-scale concentration around the Coma (A1656) and Leo (A1367) clusters; identified as the Coma/A1367 supercluster by Gregory & Thompson 1978 (ApJ 222, 784).
A mid-distance overdensity in the Hydra–Centaurus direction; CF-4 shows a sustained 99.5th+ percentile density peak at this location, consistent with a ~50 Mpc-wide wall.
A 50–70 Mpc-scale supercluster spanning A2147, A2151, and A2152; Einasto et al. 2001 (AJ 122, 2222) place the characteristic scale at 50–70 Mpc.
The densest cluster concentration in the local universe; ~25 Abell cluster members spanning ~40 Mpc at ~195 Mpc (Quintana et al. 2000, AJ 120, 511).
A prominent supercluster at ~290 Mpc anchored by the merging clusters A2061, A2065, A2067, and A2089; well-studied at intermediate redshift (Small et al. 1998, ApJ 505, 506).
One of the most extended structures within 300 Mpc, stretching ~150 Mpc from Pisces through Cetus; identified by Tully 1987 as a major supercluster complex.
A nearby void just south of the celestial equator; ~25 Mpc characteristic radius. Sharp 1986 (MNRAS 221, 137); size approximate due to void-finding method sensitivity.
Adjacent to the Local Group, extending mostly above the galactic plane; Tully et al. 2008 (ApJ 676, 184) place the centre near (l=37°, b=15°) at ~25 Mpc, with an effective radius of ~30 Mpc.
The 'Great Void' of Kirshner et al. (1981, 1987); ~50 Mpc radius centred at ~245 Mpc, subtending ~12° on the sky. Near the edge of the CF-4 reliable reconstruction volume.
